skills.title: Clean Code
skills.summary: Keep changes small, named for intent, and free of ceremony that only restates the code.
does: Prefer the simplest readable implementation over new helpers, types, or wrappers.
Keep behavior next to the data it belongs to.
Leave comments out unless the user asks for them.
skills.body: We use this skill when editing production code so helpers, types, and wrappers appear only when they are reused.
skills.usedWhen: Refactors, reviews, and any pull request that should stay readable.

skills.title: React Best Practices
skills.summary: Avoid waterfalls, keep bundles lean, and render only what the page needs.
does: Import modules directly instead of barrels.
Keep list UIs and page data cheap to render.
Avoid extra client state and layout-fighting animations.
skills.body: Frontend work on arg.software follows the same performance rules we apply for client SPAs: direct imports, no extra client state, and animations that do not fight layout.
skills.usedWhen: New pages, list UIs, and anything that ships in the public React bundle.

skills.title: Architecture First
skills.summary: Domain stays small. HTTP, crypto, and persistence stay outside it.
does: Keep controllers as HTTP adapters only.
Put business work in use cases with explicit constructor dependencies.
Map database rows in repositories, not in domain objects.
skills.body: Backend changes follow the existing admin and RAG layout: controllers orchestrate HTTP, use cases own the work, repositories map rows.
skills.usedWhen: Admin APIs, RAG pipelines, and any new backend feature.

skills.title: Domain Modeling
skills.summary: Model real invariants, not database columns or request DTOs.
does: Keep only real business invariants in domain objects.
Do not invent mapper layers or Partial inputs for a single call.
Preserve source data instead of silently normalizing it.
skills.body: New types appear when the business needs them. We do not invent mapper layers or Partial inputs for a single call.
skills.usedWhen: Outreach, visits, sessions, and other admin domain objects.

skills.title: SEO Prerender
skills.summary: Every public route gets prerendered HTML, sitemap entries, and matching SPA meta.
does: Add both slash variants of a route.
Keep SPA SEO, STATIC_PAGES, and redirects in sync.
Prerender one HTML file per public URL.
skills.body: New pages are wired in routes, STATIC_PAGES, redirects, and page SEO together so crawlers and the SPA stay in sync.
skills.usedWhen: Adding a public page or changing copy that appears in search.

skills.title: Security Hardening
skills.summary: Rate limits, origin checks, and encrypted fields stay at the right layer.
does: Rate-limit public write endpoints at the controller.
Keep secrets out of analytics, logs, and the repo.
Encrypt sensitive outreach fields at rest.
skills.body: Public writes are limited at the controller. Secrets never land in analytics or the repo.
skills.usedWhen: Login, visit logging, assistant asks, and outreach storage.

skills.title: RAG Assistant
skills.summary: Gaspar answers from ingested first-party sources, not guesses.
does: Ingest new site content so the assistant stays current.
Keep retrieval strategies in application code.
Keep loaders and file formats in infrastructure.
skills.body: New site content is ingested so the assistant stays current. Retrieval stays in application strategies; loaders stay in infrastructure.
skills.usedWhen: Publishing pages, posts, or JSON the assistant should know.

skills.title: Writing Plans
skills.summary: Agree the shape of a change before touching files.
does: Name the files, UX, and out-of-scope work first.
Keep dummy copy until the layout is agreed.
Use a branch for work that is not ready for main.
skills.body: Larger work starts with a short plan: files, UX, and what is out of scope. This page itself started that way.
skills.usedWhen: New pages, data jobs, and anything that needs a branch first.
